pr_title: STJ: Support serialization callbacks for collection and dictionary types

issue_context.title: System.Text.Json serialization callbacks not supported by collection types
issue_context.body: The System.Text.Json [serialization callbacks](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.text.json.serialization.ijsononserializing?view=net-6.0) are currently not supported by collection/dictionary converters, even though they could be. The [newly released callback APIs](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/71123) in the System.Text.Json contract model reflect that behavior, but we should consider changing that in the future.

review_comments:
One case to consider is handling of immutable collections such as `ImmutableArray<T>` and `ImmutableDictionary<K,V>`. These use an intermediate mutable collection that is converted to the final result via the `ConvertCollection` helper method. 

I don't think it would make sense to call the `OnDeserializing` callback with the intermediate builder since it would be passing in a wrong type. My gut tells me that only `OnDeserialized` should be supported in such cases (throwing an InvalidOperationException if users try to set `OnDeserializing`).

I would recommend taking a look at how the constructor-based converter handles `OnDeserializing` since it's fairly similar to immutable collections in that respect.

> I would recommend taking a look at how the constructor-based converter handles OnDeserializing since it's fairly similar to immutable collections in that respect.

It would appear that it does invoke it right after the constructor has been invoked:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8366f6ad79645de6543ccfb006812ae461e4132e/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Serialization/Converters/Object/ObjectWithParameterizedConstructorConverter.cs#L61-L63

In the case of immutable collections that would translate to calling both `OnDeserializing` and `OnDeserialized` at the same location. Given that this differs from mutable collections, I would be inclined to simply reject `OnDeserializing` callbacks for the case of immutable collections.

I fully adhere to your reasoning, but immutable collections and dictionaries (from `System.Collections.Immutable`) cannot have callbacks as they are all _sealed_ types.
Do I miss something here?
You can still install them via the `JsonTypeInfo.OnDeserializing` property which is public.

If you're looking for ways to do this, one possibility is exposing a boolean flag on `JsonConverter` and have the immutable collection converters set it. The `OnDeserializing` setter can then check for that and reject if necessary.

I have reused the `IsImmutableEnumerableType` and `IsImmutableDictionaryType` extension methods, which are the ones used to select the specific converters for immutable collections/dictionaries.
It should not impact performance significantly as it does not seem used in a hot path.
Could you also add a few tests in MetadataTests.cs that verify that callbacks can be specified via the `JsonTypeInfo` APIs?
